en: "Jeratan's gonna splurge!{w}Jeratan will get a really good prize ready!{w}Jeratan is totally satisfied!"{w}
"Munch munch...{w}Yummy!{w}These sweets go great with tea!"{w}
"Jeratan will get a prize ready that's a little bit good!{w}It's Jeratan's way of saying thank you!"{w}
"Hmm.{w}Is this really a sweet?"{w}{p}"Chomp...{w}Crunch... crunch..."{w}
"It's... yucky.{w}It's so yucky it made Jeratan cry."{w}
note: mazui lisped as majui; rendered as childish "yucky" rather than a phonetic lisp.

en: "Jeratan's happy to get a sweet Jeratan never had before, but...{w}next time, Jeratan wants you to make sure it tastes good too.{w}Jeratan will get a so-so prize ready."{w}

"Hmph!{w}Why a sweet bun, of all things?!{w}You bought that right here, didn't you?!!"{w}{p}"...Jeratan will eat it, though.{w}Munch munch...{w}It's yummy, but... munch munch..."{w}{p}"With something like this, Jeratan can't give you much of a prize. Don't get your hopes up, okay?"{w}
note: amashoku (a domed sweet bun sold in this shop) = "sweet bun"; same item as ITEM.CSV:494.

en: "D-did you say dynamite?!{w}Look out, everybody take cover!!"{w}
"Hellooo~"{w}
"Oh, it's the Pwincipal!"{w}
note: kouchou-sensei in babytalk -> "Pwincipal". Principal's gender unknown (glossary): no Mister/Ms.

en: Principal
"I've come to buy some more sweet buns, you seeee~{w}They're a favorite of the fairy folk, you knooow~{w}Sn-snort! Snort-ho-ho!!"{w}
note: buhyo = pig-snort laugh, rendered as "snort" throughout (Jera calls the Principal a pig in 5715).

en: "P-Pwincipal, run away, quick!"{w}
"Yeees~? What is it~???{w}What's the matter, everyone, all in a panic like that... snort-hee."{w}
"No good, the Principal's too much of a pig to make it in time!{w}We'll just have to get ourselves to safety!!"{w}
note: Subject restored: the Principal (bare "too piggy to make it"). buta-sugite kept at full rudeness as "too much of a pig". "watashi-tachi dake demo" = at least we ourselves.

en: "Mmm... is this an evacuation driiill~?{w}My, how admirable~ What was it again, ahh... yes, PIE!"{w}
note: Pun adapted: Japanese school-drill mnemonic OKASHI (don't push / run / talk) doubles as "sweets". English uses the acronym PIE (a sweet) with the joke third rule "don't Expire" (= the Principal's "don't die"). See 5721.

en: "Come on, Jeratan!!"{w}
"P, don't Push... I, don't get Impatient...{w}E, don't Expire... when I say that, you seeee~{w}the students all just love it~ Snort!"{w}
note: Source: [O] don't push, [KA] don't run, [SHI] don't die. Adapted to PIE; "don't run" became "don't get Impatient" to fit the letter I; "don't die" kept as "don't Expire".

en: "The Pwincipal... the Pwincipal's gonna...!!"{w}
note: Source trails off: "Teacher is, teacher is~!!"

You really feel like you're making something!"{w}{p}"The weapons and armor we put our hearts into get used by people all across the land, and they do some good!"{w}{p}"There's no job more worthwhile than this!{w}Gahahahahaha!!"{w}

"What the hell?!{w}Don't go hoarding more stuff than you can carry!"{w}{p}"You're short on pockets, pockets!{w}Go tell your ma to sew you some more!!"{w}

"Kasu -- that means 'junk' -- the perfect sword for the likes of you right now.{w}If you want a stronger sword, get your hands on the Miyoshino Tarot!"{w}{p}"The Miyoshino Tarot --{w}once you've got it, bring it here!"{w}
note: Hanafuda yaku names (Kasu, Miyoshino, Akayoroshi, Inoshikacho, Omote-Sugawara, Ameshiko, Goko) are the sword names, romanized. kasu also means "dregs/trash"; Garian puns on it, so the meaning is glossed in the line.

en: "Once you've got the Miyoshino Tarot, bring it here along with the Kasu sword!"{w}
"Alright, the Miyoshino!{w}Good work. Now, hand over the Kasu!"{w}{p}"...Hey, you over here! Temper this sword!"{w}
note: Garian calls a different smith each time: kocchi/socchi/acchi/mukou/dareka -> over here / over there / way over there / at the far end / somebody.

en: "It's done -- the Miyoshino!{w}But this sword can still be tempered a lot more!"{w}{p}"Next, bring me the Akayoroshi Tarot!"{w}
note: dekita zo, Miyoshino: the name is the finished sword, not an address.

en: "Once you've got the Akayoroshi Tarot, bring it here along with the Miyoshino sword!"{w}
"Alright, the Akayoroshi!{w}Good work. Now, hand over the Miyoshino!"{w}{p}"...Hey, you over there! Temper this sword!"{w}

"It's done -- the Akayoroshi!{w}But this sword can still be tempered a lot more!"{w}{p}"Next, bring me the Boar & Bush Clover, Deer & Maple and Butterfly & Peony Tarots!{w}I'll temper it into the Inoshikacho!!"{w}
note: Hanafuda card names translated (they are item names, ITEM.CSV:499-507, max 20 chars).
